newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell Singapore to extend crude run cut into Aug.
newsitem.headline: Shell Singapore to extend crude run cut into Aug.

text.p: Shell Singapore said on Tuesday it will extend a cut in crude runs of about 15 percent into August at its 59,000-tonne-per day (TPD) (435,000-barrel-per-day) refinery.
"The plan is to continue crude runs at a reduced in-take," a company spokeswoman said. She said the length of the cut will depend on "market conditions."
Shell annouced a 9,000-TPD cut in output on June 27 after the refinery recorded losses following a plunge in key product prices such as gas oil.
Industry sources said Esso Singapore had cut output at its 230,000-bpd refinery by about 10-percent in late June as well but a company spokeswoman declined to comment.
Traders said margins have since improved to give a profit of under 50 cents for every barrel refined at the basic stage but market outlook remains bleak due to poor regional demand.
"On paper, margins have improved, but there is a big negative premium right now for gas oil," one trader said. Gas oil is currently sold at about 50 cents below current spot Singapore prices.
Shell plans to shutdown its 11,000-TPD thermal gas oil complex for 21 days from early August.
